spec.name: Leads Landing Page
spec.type: Marketing landing page with lead-capture contact form
spec.stack: Next.js (App Router, React, TypeScript) fullstack — public landing page + a server-side API route handling the contact form; Prisma ORM persisting leads to a PostgreSQL database on the Azure VM. Deployed to the Azure VM (DJANGO-PROJECT / django-vm) via the deterministic infra/deploy.sh pipeline (firewall rotated via control plane, rsync+build as user mostafa over SSH), served behind the existing Nginx + systemd setup. Built entirely inside the project's own localPath folder.
spec.description: Build a SMALL landing page with a contact form that saves leads to a database (owner's literal requirement: 'rep 8' — preserved verbatim as the owner stated it, applied as instructed). DEPLOY it when finished. Explicit owner constraint: NO QA agent for this project. Objective: a single, lightweight marketing landing page (hero/value section + a contact form capturing lead fields such as name, email, message) whose form submissions are persisted as lead records in a database, then the finished site is deployed. Platform/decisions: Next.js (App Router + TypeScript) as a fullstack app — the landing page is server-rendered React; the contact form POSTs to a Next.js API route that validates input and writes a Lead row via Prisma to PostgreSQL. Database runs on the Azure VM; schema managed with Prisma using `prisma migrate deploy` only (additive, never migrate dev/reset on the VM). Deploy via infra/deploy.sh + infra/deploy.config.sh — firewall (port 22 single-IP) refreshed through the Azure control plane, then rsync/build/restart as user mostafa over SSH (NEVER as root); 80/443 kept open; secrets (.env*, .backup-env, *.pem, *.key, config/*.json) always excluded from sync. All scaffolding and files live inside the project's own localPath folder (to be set before build) — never in the Odin repo root. Deploy is gated behind owner approval and ODIN_ALLOW_PROD_DEPLOY as applicable; after deploy the site is polled until HTTP 200 and the result reported. No QA agent is staffed per owner instruction.
features: Responsive single landing page (hero + value/CTA sections)
Contact form with fields (name, email, message) and client+server-side validation
Next.js API route that receives form submissions, validates, and stores them
Lead model persisted to a PostgreSQL database via Prisma (one row per submission)
Success / error feedback to the visitor after submitting
Prisma schema + additive migration (`migrate deploy`) for the leads table
Production build and deploy to the Azure VM via infra/deploy.sh, served behind Nginx/systemd
Post-deploy health check polled until HTTP 200

features.name: Spam protection (honeypot or rate limiting) on the form
features.why: A public contact form will attract bot submissions; a lightweight honeypot/rate-limit keeps the leads table clean without adding a third-party dependency.

features.name: Lead notification email/HubSpot sync
features.why: Owner has HubSpot and Klaviyo connected — pushing each captured lead to HubSpot (or emailing it) makes the leads actionable instead of only sitting in the DB. Not built unless approved.

features.name: Simple CSV/admin export of leads
features.why: Gives the owner a way to actually read/use captured leads without opening the database directly.

members.name: Designer
members.why: A landing page's conversion depends heavily on visual polish; a Designer would improve the hero/layout beyond a developer's default styling. Optional — Fullstack can ship a clean standard design without one.

members.name: Security
members.why: Public form + stored PII (emails) has a small attack surface (injection, spam, data exposure). Optional given the small scope, but worth a review if lead data is sensitive.
